protection.title: Privacy and protection
protection.name: Protected identity
protection.explain: If you have protected personal data (in Sweden: skyddade personuppgifter, sekretessmarkering or skyddad folkbokföring), or for another good reason, turn on protected identity.
protection.othersDont: Other members no longer see you anywhere: not in rosters, the register, activities or answers.
protection.whoSees: Your family, the club's managers and registrars and your own leaders still see you, with a crossed-out camera: they must not photograph, film, publish or share anything about you.
protection.addressDeleted: Any address stored about you is deleted and none can be stored.
protection.turnOffConsequences: Other members will see you again in rosters, the register and activities. You need to have logged in in the last 15 minutes.
protection.removalRefused: Only the guardian who turned it on can turn it off. Talk to the other guardian or to the club.
protection.protectYourself: Protect yourself too? Your name can reveal your child.
protection.guardianHint: Your child has protected identity, but you do not. Your name can reveal your child.
protection.addChildHint: Other members will not see the child, and no address is stored.
protection.accessLogIntro: Every time someone else opens the profile of a person with protected identity, or any profile in a club that logs every view, it is noted here: when, in which club and who.
protection.logEmpty: Nobody else has opened this profile.

sources.global: Protected by the person or their family
sources.both: Protected by the family and in the club

protection.clubTurnedOn: The member is now protected in the club.
protection.clubHint: Use this when the family has told the club. A second factor is needed; every club manager is told (without the name).
protection.protectedMembersIntro: Members with protected identity, from the person or family or set in the club. Brief the leaders: no photos, films, publishing or sharing.
protection.modeHint: When every view is logged, each member can see who opened their profile, and the profile pages say so. Views of protected members are always logged.
protection.viewsLogged: Views of profiles are logged: the person can see who opened their profile.
protection.helpWhat: A crossed-out camera next to a name means that the person has protected identity. Some families have protected personal data, for example because someone is at risk: then where they are and who they are with must not spread.
protection.helpRules: Do not photograph or film the person, do not publish or share pictures, names or results, and do not tell others where and when they train or play.
protection.helpLeaders: As a leader you see the person so you can run your group. Others in the club do not see them. If you are unsure, ask the club's managers.
protection.helpView: Opening the profile of a person with protected identity is logged: the person and their guardians can see who did.

rolesAdmin.helpPermissionText: Something one may do, for example see the member register or plan the group's activities.
rolesAdmin.helpRoleText: A name for a set of permissions, for example Treasurer or Head coach.
rolesAdmin.helpPersonText: Gets the role in the whole club or in a group, and may then do what the role allows.
rolesAdmin.helpGroups: A group role applies in the group where it is given, not in its subgroups. Give the role in every group where the person should have it. Group owners always keep their rights in the subgroups too.
rolesAdmin.helpManagers: Club managers always see which members have protected identity, but not their details, unless they also hold a role that gives them. That is needed to find every member and give them roles.
rolesAdmin.helpSelf: Whoever administers roles may give any role, also to themselves. It shows on the roles page and the other administrators and the chair are told.
rolesAdmin.helpEffect: A change applies at once: the next time someone with the role opens a page, the new permissions decide. Those who lose a permission get a notice.

administrators.title: Administrators
administrators.intro: Administrators run the club and decide who may do what. A club needs at least two, so that it is never left without one and nobody alone can take it over. Three are recommended.
administrators.neededTitle: The club cannot take new members
administrators.neededBody: It has fewer than two administrators. Everything else works as usual: existing members, activities and logins are unaffected.
administrators.graceBody: A club must have at least two. After that the club cannot take new members until it has two.
administrators.recommendThird: The club has two administrators. With three, two of them can suspend the third without outside help, for example after a break-in.

administrators.howMinimum: With fewer than two administrators the club cannot take new members. Someone cannot leave the role if fewer than two would remain.
administrators.howCounts: The permission can be in several roles. Only adults with their own account count.
administrators.howThird: Three are recommended: then two can suspend the third without help.
administrators.howSuspend: A suspension is asked for by one administrator and confirmed by another (or the chair when the club has two). With two and the chair concerned, the platform's operator helps through the documented procedure.
administrators.howAdd: Every administrator and the chair are told when someone becomes an administrator. One administrator is enough to appoint another.

clubTypes.newTypeHint: The type starts with the roles every type needs: club manager, chair and the participant role.

chatHelp.title: How chat works
chatHelp.intro: In chat you can talk with your team and your leaders. Here is what applies, so that everyone feels safe.

children.title: If you are a child
children.body:
You can chat with your teammates and make your own channels with them.
If a leader or another adult writes to you, your parents always join the same chat. No adult may be alone with you in a chat.
Your parents can see which chats you are in. If they join, everyone in the chat sees it.
If something feels wrong, scary or mean: tap “Report”. The person you report will not know it was you. You can also always talk to a parent or leader you trust.

parents.title: For parents
parents.body: On the family page you see which chats your child is in and who is in them. You read the messages only if you join the chat – everyone there then sees that you joined. When a leader or another adult is in a chat with children, the children's parents are added automatically, with the whole history.

leaders.title: For leaders
leaders.body: Write to players in the team's channels. If you write directly to a child, the child's parents are added to the chat. Other adults cannot start a chat with someone else's child. If the club requires a criminal record check, you need a valid one to write to children.

reports.title: Reporting
reports.body: Anyone can report a message or a whole chat with one tap. The report goes to the club's safeguarding officers, never to the person reported.

officers.title: For safeguarding officers
officers.body: You see who reported, why and which message – not the chat. To read the chat you ask and another safeguarding officer confirms; then you may both read for a day and every read is logged. The club therefore needs at least two safeguarding officers. You can hide messages, mute someone in the club's chats for a time and close the case; the person concerned is told.

kept.title: What is kept
kept.body: Messages are kept as long as the chat exists. A message you delete is hidden but kept, and earlier versions of edited messages are kept – the club's record if something happens. Notifications of new messages never show the text or who wrote it. Messages older than three years are shown only to those in the chat.
